items.q: In what three dimensions do we map people we love?
items.a: **Space** (physical proximity), **time** (temporal proximity), and **closeness** (emotional distance). The **inferior parietal lobule** tracks changes across those dimensions.

items.q: What is grief doing to that map?
items.a: Grief is **uncoupling** attachment from **space/time predictions** (they'll walk in, call at the usual hour). Adaptive grieving **keeps the attachment**; dismantling the bond is not the goal.

items.q: How do you practice rational grieving in a session?
items.a: Dedicate **5–45 minute blocks** (often 5–10–30+) to feel attachment deeply while consciously decoupling from spatial/temporal seeking — **accept the new reality** and still **anchor to the bond**.

items.q: Why avoid "what if" thinking during those blocks?
items.a: **Counterfactual thinking** is an **infinite guilt landscape** tightly tied to guilt. Rational grieving means clear acceptance plus attachment — not spiraling "what if I had…" loops.

items.q: Does more yearning mean you loved more deeply?
items.a: Not necessarily. **Oxytocin receptor density** in the nucleus accumbens (prairie vole + human fMRI) links to **intense yearning/motivation to reconnect**, not greater attachment capacity.

items.q: Does bereavement writing help everyone equally?
items.a: A **35-subject** study found **no group effect** until stratified by **vagal tone / RSA** — high respiratory sinus arrhythmia writers (who can feel attachment somatically) benefited most.

items.q: How does complicated grief show up in cortisol?
items.a: **Complicated grief** keeps **4 PM and 9 PM cortisol elevated** vs non-complicated patterns. Foundation tools: **morning sunlight** to normalize diurnal cortisol plus sleep hygiene.

items.q: When does the remapping actually consolidate?
items.a: Neuroplasticity is trigger + offline wiring: remapping consolidates in **sleep** and **10–30 min NSDR**. Grief differs from **depression** despite overlapping symptoms (sleep, appetite, crying); Kübler-Ross stages are **partial**, not universal — craving circuits dominate on fMRI.
